rejected.title: What a market is
card: A market is any place or way that buyers and sellers come together to trade. Buyers want to get goods or services. Sellers want to sell them.
A market can be a place you visit, such as a weekend food market. It can also be online, such as a website that sells shoes.
A market does not need a building. The share market is a market because people buy and sell shares in companies there.
What makes something a market is that buyers and sellers meet to trade, whether face to face, by phone or on the internet.
rejected.remember: A market is where buyers and sellers trade, in person or online.

a.q: Which example shows buyers and sellers in a market?
opts: An app where people buy and sell used bikes
A bike left unused in a garage
A bike shop's list of staff wages
A bike race held on a Sunday morning
a.why: On the app, buyers and sellers come together to trade bikes, so it is a market. A race has riders but no buying and selling of goods, so it is not a market.
a.clue: Look for buyers and sellers who trade.

b.q: Zane sells handmade candles. Which choice shows him selling in a market?
opts: Selling candles to customers on a website
Making candles at home for himself
Giving candles to his family as gifts
Buying wax and keeping it in a cupboard
b.why: Selling candles to customers on a website brings a seller and buyers together to trade, so it is a market. Making candles for himself or giving them away involves no trade with buyers.
b.clue: Which choice has a seller trading with buyers?

version.title: What a market is
card: A market is any place or way that buyers and sellers come together to trade goods or services.
Some markets are in one place, such as a weekend farmers market. Others are online, such as a website that sells second-hand clothes.
A market does not need a building. On the share market, people buy and sell parts of companies, called shares, mostly through computers.
To tell whether something is a market, ask: are buyers and sellers trading? Where or how they meet does not matter.
version.remember: If buyers and sellers are trading, it is a market, wherever and however they meet.

a.q: Which statement about markets is correct?
opts: A market can exist without any building at all
A market needs a building where people meet
A market trades only goods, never services
A market is a place where goods are made to sell
a.why: Buyers and sellers can trade online or by phone, so a market does not need a building. A building is tempting because many markets have one, but the share market trades mostly through computers.

b.q: Jai says the share market is not a real market, because nobody meets face to face. Is he right?
opts: No, buyers and sellers still trade shares
Yes, a market needs buyers and sellers to meet
Yes, shares are not goods, so they have no market
No, the share market meets in one building daily
b.why: Buyers and sellers still come together to trade shares, so it is a market. They do not need to meet face to face, because where or how they meet does not matter.
b.clue: What has to happen for something to be a market?

a.best: A market can exist without any building at all

b.best: No, buyers and sellers still trade shares

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedging qualifier ("can"), while two wrong options use absolutes ("needs", "only ... never"). A test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea. Reword so the options are alike in tone, for example make the right option a plain statement such as "A market is buyers and sellers trading, wherever they meet" or remove the absolutes from the wrong ones.
